# Skills

Five independently installable skills: three primary areas and two retained
compatibility entrypoints. This README covers the skills maintained in this
repository, not unrelated host-bundled or plugin skills.

- **`/develop`** — Iterate or explicit BDD, specifications, prompt changes, requirement coverage, and repository validation.
- **`/review`** — Code/current-source review, structural audit, or technical discussion; single-pass unless Debate is explicitly selected.
- **`/research report create|update`** — Saved-evidence assembly and maintenance through an existing report pipeline; not new research.
- **`/iterate`** and **`/debate`** retain their arguments and canonical methods as compatibility entrypoints.

Each exported folder contains its full resources without sibling installations.
Debate is optional, not an Iterate gate. Model references are not a whitelist;
prefer economical capable reviewers, stronger middle-stage models and strongest
final synthesis within available host/data/tool/budget permissions.

Installation/metadata checks do not certify host invocation or model quality.
See `evaluations/status.json` for unperformed gates; full acceptance is not claimed.

## Skill catalog

[`inventory.json`](inventory.json) defines the exported skills, methods and shared
resources. All five are discoverable through this checkout's `.agents/skills/`
links; each can also be installed on its own from a complete exported bundle.

| Skill | Available modes | Canonical instructions |
|---|---|---|
| `develop` | `iterate`, `bdd`, `prd`, `prompt`, `backlog`, `validate-repo` | [Develop](develop/SKILL.md) |
| `review` | `code`, `smells`, `discuss`; `single` or explicit `debate` engine | [Review](review/SKILL.md) |
| `research` | `report create`, `report update` | [Research reports](research/SKILL.md) |
| `iterate` | Feature creation/resumption, phase selection, `park`, `list` | [Iterate](iterate/SKILL.md) |
| `debate` | Explicit hierarchical `review` or `discuss` | [Debate](debate/SKILL.md) |

Develop includes the canonical Iterate method and helper; Review includes the
canonical Debate method. Installing either parent does not require installing
its compatibility entrypoint. Shared policies, host mappings, project profiles,
worked examples and composition guidance travel with every exported skill.

### Code review or smell audit?

| Mode | Use when | Result | Do not use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `review code` | Assessing whether a supplied change or declared current implementation is desirable, correctly placed, correct and maintainable. | Findings with evidence, preferred remedies, urgency, compatibility implications and review coverage. | Implementing fixes or automatically auditing the whole repository. |
| `review smells` | Investigating structures that make a declared subsystem or repository harder to maintain, change, test or operate. | Consequence-grounded structural findings, a file coverage ledger and dependency-aware remediation plan. | Size/style criticism alone or automatically performing a refactor. |

For a concrete example, `/review code src/importer.py --scope source` asks whether
the current importer is acceptable. `/review smells src/importing` asks which
structural problems make that subsystem difficult to change and in what order
to address them. Both are read-only; recommending a fix does not apply it. Asking
"What is a code smell?" calls for an explanation, not either review workflow.

Provide a target and accessible source; include the real base for diff review and
prior findings for re-review. Missing sources remain unreviewed. Current-source
review without a base cannot establish when a defect was introduced. Review stops
at the requested report, including valid no-finding results and unperformed checks.

The skill requires reading the full selected method:
[code-review checklist and finding contract](review/references/code.md) or
[structural diagnostic patterns and report contract](review/references/smells.md).
The [source coverage map](review/references/source-coverage.md) traces the methods
to the supplied materials. The Python source is a historical report, not its
separately referenced smell guide; old findings and project assumptions are not
current facts. Detailed guidance stays in the selected reference.

## Which skill should I use?

Choose by the outcome you need next, not by how many skills are installed. These
skills add working discipline: development controls how a change is made, review
challenges evidence and decisions without editing, and report work protects claims
while assembling saved results. They are not five steps that every task must follow.

For new work, start with `develop`, `review` or `research`. Use `iterate` and
`debate` directly when you want their existing standalone entrypoints; they do not
add capabilities missing from the corresponding parents.

| What you need now | Choose | Why and when it helps | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Build a feature whose behavior or ergonomics needs hands-on feedback | `/develop iterate <feature>` or `/iterate <feature>` | You need to agree on architecture, try a minimal end-to-end flow and refine it before stabilizing tests. This is the default feature-development lifecycle. | An implemented flow, a manual test bed, integration tests and explicitly tracked deferred work, with user checkpoints. |
| Fix or add precisely specified behavior using test-first development | `/develop bdd <task>` | You can describe an observable acceptance outcome, or the project explicitly requires red-before-code. A duplicate-delivery bug is a typical case. | A genuine failing behavioral test, the minimum implementation and a verified green result. |
| Decide what an implementer should build, without building it yet | `/develop prd <target>` | The desired outcome exists, but contracts, compatibility, failure behavior or acceptance criteria need a complete developer handoff. | A preferred design and implementation specification with bounded unresolved decisions. |
| Change a generation prompt without breaking its consumers | `/develop prompt <target>` | Prompt meaning also appears in schemas, examples, validation or replay; changing wording alone could leave those surfaces inconsistent. | Coordinated authorized prompt/contract edits, checked within the chosen lifecycle. |
| Find out whether requirements are actually delivered and owned | `/develop backlog <scope>` | Tickets, enabling infrastructure and user-visible completion do not clearly line up. Use it before inventing more work or duplicate owners. | An evidence-linked coverage register separating delivered, partial, missing and unknown work. |
| Check whether a repository change is locally ready | `/develop validate-repo [scope]` | You need the project's actual tests/checks, prerequisites and final-change inspection, rather than another design opinion. | Check results, failures and blockers; not a deployment or permission to fix everything. |
| Look for actionable defects in a change or current source | `/review code <target>` | You want an independent source-grounded assessment of correctness, compatibility and implementation choices before accepting or revising code. | Findings with evidence, preferred remedies, urgency and coverage; no edits. |
| Understand why a subsystem is difficult or risky to change | `/review smells <scope>` | Repeated policies, coupled state or scattered responsibilities have a concrete maintenance or behavioral consequence. Use an explicit structural scope, not a file-length quota. | Consequence-grounded structural findings and a dependency-aware remedy plan; no refactoring. |
| Choose between technical alternatives | `/review discuss <topic>` | You need to challenge a decision such as synchronous versus queued import, compare real tradeoffs and identify evidence that could change the recommendation. | A supported preferred decision, conditional claims and consequential unknowns; no implementation. |
| Assemble or revise a report from results you already have | `/research report create|update <target>` | Approved saved evidence and an existing report build pipeline are available, and claims, provenance, uncertainty or privacy must survive the edits. | A built/updated report with actual evidence and acceptance-check status; no new research. |
| Explicitly request independent challenge and reconciliation | Add `--engine debate` to a review mode, or use `/debate review|discuss ...` | A consequential decision or disputed finding warrants the additional nine-agent process and its resource cost. This is optional, not the default for ordinary review. | Five independent reviews, three whole-set reconciliations and one evidence-checked synthesis, subject to actual host capability. |

If you only need a simple answer or a small document edit, a full development
lifecycle or hierarchical review may add nothing. Use the smallest applicable
method, and stop when the requested answer or authorized handoff is complete.

### Where the purposes overlap

- **Develop and Iterate:** `/develop iterate` uses the same canonical lifecycle as
  `/iterate`, including phase selection, `park` and `list`. Choose one entrypoint;
  do not run both as separate workflows for the same feature. Develop additionally
  exposes specification, BDD, prompt, coverage and validation modes.
- **Review and Debate:** Debate is an execution engine for explicitly selected
  review/discussion, not another kind of implementation work. Review defaults to
  single-pass and adds scope/engine controls. Do not run a completed Debate again
  through the other entrypoint just to get a second version of the same analysis.
- **Iterate and BDD:** both implement and verify behavior, but their sequencing
  differs. Iterate refines behavior through manual feedback before its testing
  phase; BDD demonstrates behavioral red before production changes. Select one
  lifecycle, not both. Given/When/Then wording does not turn Iterate into BDD.
- **PRD, architecture and discussion:** all can compare designs. Discussion owns
  the decision analysis; PRD owns a complete implementation handoff; Iterate's
  architecture phase owns direction and user agreement for an active feature.
  Reuse settled evidence instead of repeating all three. A PRD does not bypass
  Iterate's architecture checkpoint.
- **Code review and structural audit:** both inspect source and may notice the
  same duplicated policy. Code review asks whether the implementation/change is
  acceptable; a smell audit asks which structural consequences make the declared
  scope risky to maintain. A code review does not automatically become a broader
  audit, and an audit does not automatically authorize a refactor.
- **Review and repository validation:** review supplies reasoned findings;
  validation supplies results from mapped project checks and readiness inspection.
  They complement each other, but passing tests does not settle every design claim
  and a persuasive review does not mean checks ran.
- **Requirement coverage and Iterate's deferred work:** `develop backlog` maps
  requirements to delivery evidence and owners. Iterate's local queue tracks
  concerns deferred within a feature. Neither is a replacement for the other;
  they are not automatically synchronized.
- **Prompt editing and development:** prompt guidance specializes affected
  contracts inside the same authorized executor and lifecycle. It is not a second
  feature workflow, and contract tests do not prove generation accuracy.
- **Research reports and discussion/validation:** report work owns evidence,
  provenance, report edits and report acceptance. Discussion can challenge an
  interpretation; repository validation can check changed supporting code. Neither
  supplies missing evidence or replaces report-specific checks. Despite its name,
  `research` does not conduct new research or build a new report pipeline.

## Current qualification

The recorded status in [`evaluations/status.json`](evaluations/status.json) is:

- Deterministic checks, temporary Codex/Claude layout installation and composition
  documentation/packaging checks: passed.
- Real host installation/discovery, invocation and hierarchy checks: not run.
- Manual acceptance, model quality, reference fidelity, transfer and composition
  model behavior: not run.
- Release, model-protocol and composition-protocol approval: pending.

Recorded limits include unavailable private historical artifacts and the separately
referenced Python smell guide, plus blocked browser visual inspection. These records
are not proof of current live host behavior. Stable release readiness also requires
acceptance evidence matching the current source-resource fingerprint.

## Install

### Another project: use the zip

Download a versioned skill zip and its checksum from a trusted release, open your
target project and ask its agent: **“install the skills in this zip file.”**
Choose `skills-<tag>.zip`, not GitHub's automatic source-code archive. The
archive's root README and manifest describe scoped installation and include an
auditable Python 3.11+ standard-library installer. Extracting a zip never autoruns
code. The agent must inspect it and retain applicable approvals.

The installer copies complete selected folders into project `.agents/skills`
for Codex or `.claude/skills` for Claude Code. It previews changes, skips identical
content, rejects conflicts/symlink escapes, and upgrades only unchanged previously
managed files when requested. No global install, hooks, settings edits, Git changes,
data acquisition or skill-workflow execution occurs.

For a local bundle from this checkout, prepare/export first, then use the audited
source installer against a different project:

```sh
.venv/bin/python scripts/build_skills.py --prepare
.venv/bin/python distribution/install.py --archive dist/skills-dev.zip --project /absolute/path/to/target --host codex --dry-run
.venv/bin/python distribution/install.py --archive dist/skills-dev.zip --project /absolute/path/to/target --host codex
```

Use `--host claude`, `--skills develop review`, or explicitly requested `--upgrade`
as appropriate. Do not point the copy installer at this checkout's authoring
symlinks. Internal hashes check integrity, not publisher authenticity; supply the
trusted external digest with `--sha256` when available.

### Local authoring

Clone the repository:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mdbecker/skills.git
cd skills
python3.11 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
.venv/bin/python scripts/build_skills.py --prepare
```

This checkout includes all five discovery links in `.agents/skills/`. Prepare the
ignored resource closures before local use. For live-linked authoring elsewhere,
link the prepared directories; portable distribution should use the zip instead:

```sh
mkdir -p /absolute/path/to/your-project/.agents/skills
ln -s /absolute/path/to/skills/develop /absolute/path/to/your-project/.agents/skills/develop
ln -s /absolute/path/to/skills/review /absolute/path/to/your-project/.agents/skills/review
ln -s /absolute/path/to/skills/research /absolute/path/to/your-project/.agents/skills/research
ln -s /absolute/path/to/skills/iterate /absolute/path/to/your-project/.agents/skills/iterate
ln -s /absolute/path/to/skills/debate /absolute/path/to/your-project/.agents/skills/debate
```

Replace the example paths with your actual checkout and project paths. If a
destination already exists, inspect it before replacing it. The links keep source
instructions current when you update this checkout; run
`scripts/build_skills.py --prepare` again to refresh their generated resources.
Copied installations are snapshots: pulling this repository does not update them.
Use the inspected bundle's installer and explicitly requested `--upgrade` for
previously managed project-local copies. The zip installer does not manage or
update user-global skill folders.

Use your skill picker or the host's supported invocation syntax. Slash examples
describe mode grammar; `$`/picker presentation does not itself certify another host.

## Area commands

```text
/develop iterate csv-import
/develop bdd reject-duplicate-delivery
/develop prd import-spec
/develop prompt invoice-extraction
/develop backlog import-requirements
/develop validate-repo
/review code src/importer.py --scope source
/review smells src/importer
/review discuss "Synchronous import or queue?" --engine debate
/research report create reliability-summary
/research report update reliability-summary
```

Explicit BDD is genuinely test-first; ordinary Iterate keeps manual feedback before
its testing stage. Drafting/review does not implement changes. Coverage registers
are separate from Iterate state. Current-source review needs no invented baseline;
changing review engine does not widen scope. Reports require saved evidence and
a mapped existing build graph; missing dependencies block work.

### Mode boundaries

- [`bdd`](develop/references/bdd.md) observes a genuine behavioral red test before
  implementing the minimum change and verifying green; import/setup failures do not
  count as red. It does not silently replace an active Iterate lifecycle.
- [`prd`](develop/references/prd.md) produces a preferred implementation design,
  contracts, acceptance scenarios and bounded unknowns, not implementation.
- [`prompt`](develop/references/prompt.md) coordinates affected generation, schema,
  validation and replay surfaces within the selected lifecycle. Deterministic
  contract validity does not establish generation quality.
- [`backlog`](develop/references/backlog.md) maps requirements, owners, implementation
  evidence and gaps in a separate coverage register; it is read-only by default and
  does not synchronize Iterate state or automatically edit trackers.
- [`validate-repo`](develop/references/validate-repo.md) checks the declared scope
  against existing project commands. Readiness inspection does not authorize fixes,
  dependency installation, formatting or live/deployed verification.
- [`code`](review/references/code.md), [`smells`](review/references/smells.md) and
  [`discuss`](review/references/discuss.md) inspect defects, consequential structure
  or a technical decision respectively. They do not implement fixes or post reviews.
- [`report create|update`](research/references/report.md) edits authoritative report
  inputs using approved saved evidence and an existing build pipeline; it does not
  acquire evidence, execute notebooks, invent results or publish deliverables.

Shared [boundaries](resources/policy.md) apply throughout. Use
[adaptation guidance](resources/adaptation.md) to map a different project's
instructions, protected contracts, permissions, prerequisites and checks; bundled
profiles are examples, not assumptions about an uninspected project.

## Combining methods when useful

Combine methods only when the second one answers a question the first does not.
Usually this means passing a finding, specification or observation to the next
authorized action, not running multiple skills concurrently. The
[optional cookbook](resources/combinations.md) gives detailed handoff, skip and
stop rules; these are not new commands or automatic pipelines.

| Situation | Useful combination | What each contributes; when to skip a step |
|---|---|---|
| A feature needs a clear handoff before implementation | `develop prd` → `develop iterate` | PRD settles the implementation contract; Iterate builds and refines it with the user. Skip a separate PRD if the existing brief is adequate. Implementation needs its own authorization and architecture agreement. |
| A change needs independent assessment and local readiness evidence | Chosen development mode → `review code` → `develop validate-repo` | Development edits; review challenges the actual change; validation runs mapped checks. Add review only for a useful requested/necessary assessment, and reuse current check evidence rather than rerunning unchanged work. |
| A ticket is done, but the user journey may be missing | `develop backlog` → optional `review code` → `develop prd`; then authorized Iterate and validation if needed | Coverage separates enabling work from delivery; source review resolves uncertain claims; PRD specifies the missing increment. Skip source review when evidence already suffices. Coverage-only or planning work stops before implementation. [C01](resources/combinations.md#c01) |
| A design choice depends on measurements you do not yet have | `review discuss` → bounded experiment brief → authorized Iterate test bed → revisit the affected decision/specification | Discussion identifies a discriminating observation; the approved experiment supplies actual evidence. Skip the experiment if existing measurements settle the question. Do not call a provisional experiment a settled production design or ship it implicitly. [C02](resources/combinations.md#c02) |
| An invoice prompt change could turn unknown into zero downstream | `develop prompt` within the active Iterate or explicitly selected BDD lifecycle; optional scoped review/validation | Prompt guidance maps field meaning and consumers; the same lifecycle/executor owns edits and testing order. Use prompt alone for a bounded wording edit; do not start both lifecycles or invent missing consumers. [C03](resources/combinations.md#c03) |
| Duplicated policies have a demonstrated failure or maintenance consequence | `review smells` → optional PRD → authorized development → scoped re-review/validation | Audit establishes the consequence; development applies the smallest complete remedy; follow-up checks test that concern. Skip PRD when the remedy is clear. Behavioral fixes can use explicit BDD; pure refactors can reuse green characterization without manufacturing red. [C04](resources/combinations.md#c04) |
| A report headline overstates what saved cohorts support | `research report create|update` + optional `review discuss`; repository validation only for affected supporting code | Report mode owns evidence, protected claims and edits; discussion tests the disputed interpretation against the same saved sources. Skip discussion when report evidence already resolves it. Neither validation nor discussion replaces visual/evidence checks or authorizes new data. [C05](resources/combinations.md#c05) |

Arrows describe possible handoffs, not permission to execute the whole chain.
Carry the target/snapshot, actual evidence, uncertainties, protected contracts,
permitted action and completion condition into the next step. Recheck consequential
claims against raw sources; reviewer agreement is not evidence.

Keep one development lifecycle and one owner of the next action. Reviewers recommend;
authorized development or report work edits. An optional second method does not
create another manifest, install missing skills, edit trackers, publish, deploy or
launch Debate. Choose `--engine debate` explicitly only when that additional
independent challenge is warranted and available.

### Combinations to avoid

- `/iterate` followed by `/develop iterate` for the same feature: two entrypoints,
  one method, not two complementary stages.
- BDD alongside Iterate to get both test sequences: conflicting lifecycle timing,
  not additional coverage. Preserve the active lifecycle unless a change is agreed.
- Ordinary review followed automatically by Debate: more agents are not a mandatory
  acceptance gate. Revisit only material new evidence or an explicitly selected need.
- PRD plus discussion plus a smell audit for every small fix: reuse a clear contract
  and remedy instead of producing redundant analysis.
- `research` to fill an evidence gap in a design experiment or report: this skill
  works with approved saved results, not data acquisition or invented measurements.
- `validate-repo` as proof a report is scientifically valid or a feature is deployed:
  repository readiness, report acceptance and live verification are different claims.

## Iterate

```text
/iterate csv-import
/iterate csv-import TWEAKING
/iterate park "Reject duplicate deliveries"
/iterate list
```

Iterate follows six phases:

1. **ARCHITECTURE:** record the impact, exclusions, data flow, and real design tradeoffs; agree on direction with the user.
2. **HAPPY_PATH:** implement the smallest useful flow and park additional concerns.
3. **TEST_BED:** provide a basic web UI and an editable Python driver, run the flow, and hand it to the user.
4. **TWEAKING:** change, run, observe, and repeat until the user says the behavior feels right.
5. **TESTING:** add a few meaningful integration tests for the stabilized flow.
6. **FINALIZATION:** address or explicitly waive deferred work one item at a time.

The bundled manifest helper requires **Python 3.11+** and uses only the standard library. Run it from the project being developed, using the installed helper's absolute path:

```sh
python3 /absolute/path/to/skills/iterate/manifest.py --help
python3 /absolute/path/to/skills/iterate/manifest.py status -v
```

State lives in that project's `.ai-state/` directory. It stays local and supports later-session resumption. The state directory and manifest files must not be symlinks. Feature-specific test-bed files stay in `testbed/scratch/`; reusable tools can be promoted to `testbed/tools/`.

The tool registry rejects linked or escaping storage at `testbed/tools/registry.json`,
including ancestor and leaf links. Explicit external tool references can still be
registered without executing them. Damaged feature state is preserved; restore a
known-good local copy under user direction rather than hand-editing or resetting it.

Git projects can use phase commits and small PRs. Local-only projects retain the same six phases and feedback checkpoints without requiring Git, a remote, or PRs. See [the full Iterate instructions](iterate/SKILL.md).

## Debate

```text
/debate review the current implementation and its diff against main
/debate review src/importer.py and its integration tests
/debate discuss "Should this import run synchronously or as a job?"
```

Debate uses actual host delegation and model availability. These are reference
selections, not required IDs or physical-size classifications:

| Stage | Agents | Reference / available alternative | Responsibility |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Independent review | 5 | `gpt-6-luna` | Complementary independent evidence inspection |
| Reconciliation | 3 | `gpt-6.1-terra` / `gpt-6.1-sol` | Each checks every candidate, counterevidence and omissions |
| Final synthesis | 1 | `gpt-6-astra` | Verify supported findings and produce the final response |

Stages run in order under observed concurrency. Same-model distinct agents are
permitted when preferred tiers are unavailable; disclose tier uncertainty instead
of falsely claiming XL qualification. Substitutions inside approved boundaries
need no repetitive model-ID approval. Missing required delegation/evidence or
incomplete stages remain blockers. No provider CLI, token setup or new runtime.

Findings must include source locations, concrete evidence or a safe reproduction, impact, severity, and the smallest reasonable fix. Agreement between reviewers is not verification. Reports distinguish verified defects, conditional claims, preferences, unresolved disagreements, and coverage limits. Cost information is reported only when available, with estimates labeled as estimates.

Reviews do not authorize code changes or publishing comments. See [the full Debate instructions](debate/SKILL.md).

## Development checks

Python 3.11+ is required. Create a development environment and run:

```sh
python3.11 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
.venv/bin/python scripts/build_skills.py --prepare
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s iterate/tests -v
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
.venv/bin/python scripts/validate_skills.py
```

The Iterate suite covers manifest and tool-registry behavior. The root suite covers
distribution, release contracts and composition guidance. Prepare resource closures
before running those suites, especially after changes to canonical resources.
Metadata checks do not prove that models will follow a skill correctly; behavioral
changes also need hands-on evaluation.

Distribution tests additionally exercise deterministic exports, installation,
standalone helpers, conflicts, upgrades, archive validation and rollback. The
protocol, evaluator-only fixtures/answers, source matrix and acceptance limits are
under `evaluations/`. Real Codex/Claude invocation and paired quality/cost checks
require their own approved evidence; they are not simulated by installer tests.

Composition checks additionally install each parent/legacy package alone in both
host layouts, verify canonical guide/anchor closure and validate frozen evaluator
criteria. They do not simulate agent route selection or certify model behavior.

## Releases

The release workflow handles an existing `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-prerelease]` tag or
manual dispatch. It verifies tagged/default-branch ancestry, runs canonical checks,
builds a clean deterministic zip/checksum, attaches assets to a draft, then publishes.
It refuses to overwrite existing releases/assets; a failed draft requires an
explicit maintainer recovery decision. No release is created by local builds.

Stable export/publication remains blocked until reviewed model/host acceptance and
approval records pass and match the current source-resource fingerprint. A tag
such as `v0.2.0-rc.1` explicitly produces a prerelease with honest qualification
metadata. Creating/pushing any tag or publishing still requires authorization.

The installation contract is in `distribution/README.md`; release automation is
defined in `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Runtime archives exclude evaluation answers,
local state, environments, credentials and restricted data.

## Layout

```text
iterate/             Development skill, manifest helper, and regression tests
debate/              Prompt-only hierarchical review skill
develop/             Development area and focused method references
review/              Single-pass scopes and explicit Debate selection
research/            Saved-evidence report assembly and maintenance
resources/           Canonical common policies, profiles, examples and provenance
distribution/        Archive README and scoped installer
evaluations/         Protocol, synthetic fixtures, evaluator answers and limits
tests/               Distribution and release-contract tests
.agents/skills/      Project-local discovery links
scripts/             Explicit resource exporter and metadata/link checks
.github/workflows/   Automated validation
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for change guidelines, [NOTICE](NOTICE) for provenance, and [LICENSE](LICENSE) for the MIT license.

Generated per-skill `resources/` and `dist/` are ignored export views; edit their
canonical sources, then prepare again. No source/helper logic is independently
maintained in those copies.

`inventory.json` controls package contents. `.github/workflows/checks.yml` runs
continuous validation; `.github/workflows/release.yml` handles authorized releases.
The `PRD*.md` files are design/acceptance references, not substitutes for current
skill instructions or recorded qualification evidence.

---
name: develop
description: Implement behavior, revise implementation specifications or prompts, reconcile requirement coverage, or validate repository changes through explicitly selected development modes. Reviews and research reports belong to their own areas.
---

# Develop

If another method would address a remaining uncertainty or contract, read only the
relevant [optional recipe](resources/combinations.md). Otherwise use this mode alone.

Select one owning mode. Load [shared boundaries](resources/policy.md), then only
the selected method and applicable project profile. The `resources/` directory
is prepared from canonical sources by the repository exporter and included in
published bundles; never substitute a sibling installation when it is missing.

| Invocation | Method |
|---|---|
| `/develop iterate <feature> [phase]` | [Existing Iterate lifecycle](resources/iterate/method.md) |
| `/develop bdd <task>` | [Test-first BDD](references/bdd.md) |
| `/develop prd <target>` | [Specification authoring](references/prd.md) |
| `/develop prompt <target>` | [Prompt/contract editing](references/prompt.md) |
| `/develop backlog <scope>` | [Requirement coverage](references/backlog.md) |
| `/develop validate-repo [scope]` | [Repository validation](references/validate-repo.md) |

Explicit mode wins. Ordinary feature implementation uses Iterate unless current
project policy explicitly selects another lifecycle. Do not turn a specification,
test review, or readiness check into implementation. Reject unknown modes with
this usage table; ask a targeted question only when consequential ambiguity
cannot be resolved from the request and project policy.

For Iterate, interpret the remaining arguments as the existing `/iterate` arguments,
including `park`, `list`, and no-argument behavior. Its bundled helper is
`resources/iterate/manifest.py`; resolve that absolute path and run it from the
target project, not the installation directory. The copied method's directory
is its helper directory. Preserve phases, manual feedback, state and user edits.
Do not change an active Iterate lifecycle merely because BDD was suggested.

Specifications choose a preferred design but do not replace Iterate's architecture
discussion and user agreement. Prompt specialization respects the selected
lifecycle's testing stage. Requirement coverage is not the deferred feature queue;
feature-state changes use the existing helper only when authorized.

For profile mapping read [adaptation](resources/adaptation.md). Relevant profiles:
[this repository](resources/profiles/skills.md), [Riskonnect](resources/profiles/riskonnect.md),
[template](resources/profiles/template.md), or the target project's own mapping.
Load the selected mode's [worked cases](resources/examples.md) only as needed.
No mode automatically invokes audits, nine-agent review, installation or deployment.

Return the selected scope, actual work/checks, results and limits. Never claim
tests, live checks, or user acceptance that did not occur.

review/SKILL.md.content:
---
name: review
description: Assess declared code changes or current implementations, audit consequential structural maintenance problems, or discuss technical decisions. Use for requested assessments, not general explanations or implementing fixes. Single-pass unless Debate is explicitly selected.
---

# Review

## Purpose and selection

Choose the assessment the user needs, not every mode that could inspect the code.

| Mode | Use when | Output | Do not use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | Assessing whether a supplied change or declared current implementation is desirable, correctly placed, correct and maintainable. | Findings with evidence, preferred remedies, urgency, compatibility implications and review coverage. | Implementing fixes or automatically auditing the whole repository. |
| `smells` | Investigating structures that make a declared subsystem or repository harder to maintain, change, test or operate. | Consequence-grounded structural findings, a file coverage ledger and dependency-aware remediation plan. | Size/style criticism alone or automatically performing a refactor. |

For example, `/review code src/importer.py --scope source` assesses the current
importer; `/review smells src/importing` audits that subsystem's structure. A
general question such as "What is a code smell?" needs an explanation, not a
source audit. A request to fix code is implementation, not read-only review;
do not substitute a review or apply a review's recommendations without authority.
Technical decision analysis remains the existing `discuss` mode.

## Inputs and completion

Establish the target, declared scope and accessible current source; read applicable
requirements, instructions, compatibility obligations and relevant supporting
callers/tests/docs. A diff assessment also needs its actual comparison base;
re-review uses supplied prior findings and revisions. Do not invent missing
sources, contracts, consumers or earlier reviews.

Use a clearly established conversational target when no explicit path is supplied.
If the target cannot be resolved, ask one targeted question instead of inspecting
an arbitrary repository. Unavailable sources are unreviewed; disclose partial
coverage and continue only independent, supportable inspection. Lack of a base
can support current-source assessment, not introduced-defect claims.

Finish when the requested report covers the declared scope, supported findings
and remedies, compatibility/uncertainty, prior dispositions when applicable,
and actual versus unperformed checks. No findings is valid. Stop there: do not
invent findings, broaden the audit, refactor, post, or start another workflow.

## Invocation and required methods

For a justified cross-method handoff, read only the relevant [optional recipe](resources/combinations.md).
It grants no edit permission, sibling dependency or automatic Debate selection.

Load [shared boundaries](resources/policy.md), then select one mode:

- `/review code <target> [--scope diff|source] [--engine single|debate]`:
  [code review](references/code.md).
- `/review smells <scope> [--engine single|debate]`:
  [structural audit](references/smells.md).
- `/review discuss <topic> [--engine single|debate]`:
  [technical discussion](references/discuss.md).

Read the selected method in full before reviewing. These references contain the
ordered checks, remedy criteria and output contracts, not optional background.
For maintenance against the original review materials, use the
[source coverage map](references/source-coverage.md); do not treat historical
findings or assumptions as facts about the current target.

Explicit arguments take precedence. Reject unknown modes, flags or values with
concise usage. Ordinary review defaults to single-pass. A supplied diff/PR uses
its established base; current-source review may proceed without a base, with
that limitation disclosed. Never invent a comparison or expand scope implicitly.
Reviewing PRD design is discussion; reviewing its implementation or the code diff
that implements a PRD is code review. Use the PRD as a contract in that code review,
not as permission to implement it.

Parse scope/engine controls before constructing the review subject. Pass only the
declared target and resolved scope to the canonical Debate method; control flags
are not source paths, shell commands or permission grants.

Scope and execution method are independent. Only explicit Debate selection loads
the [canonical hierarchy](resources/debate/method.md), [model policy](resources/models.md)
and the relevant [Codex](resources/hosts/codex.md) or [Claude](resources/hosts/claude.md)
capability mapping. This is the existing five-reviewer, three-reconciler,
one-synthesizer method, not a new orchestration runtime. Missing resources or
delegation must be reported, not replaced with a claimed completed hierarchy.

Code-review urgency, structural S0–S3 and impact severity are different dimensions.
Do not decide by agreement, invent findings to fill a quota, or call a conditional
claim verified. Inspect raw sources and consequential omissions, preserve minority
findings and unknowns, and report coverage. Use [worked cases](resources/examples.md)
and [adaptation](resources/adaptation.md) only for the chosen scope.

Review remains read-only unless fixes or posting are separately authorized.
Return the requested format, including valid JSON when requested, with actual
evidence, dispositions, preferred remedies or decisions, and unperformed checks.

# Explicit BDD

Select this lifecycle explicitly or from current project policy. Behavioral-test
review is read-only. Never activate test-first merely because ordinary feature
work mentions testing, or change an active Iterate phase without a decision.

Identify acceptance outcomes, preserved behavior and relevant negative/security
cases. Describe focused concrete Given/When/Then in domain language. Write new
behavioral tests before production changes and observe the intended red outcome;
an already-passing scenario needs investigation, not manufactured failure. An
environment/import failure is not the required behavioral failure.

Implement the minimum complete solution, preserve characterization coverage, and
observe green. Assert outputs, persisted effects and stable boundary behavior;
stub external dependencies rather than incidental internal collaborators.
Interaction assertions are valid when that interaction itself is contractual.
Keep governance/static checks separate.

Return scenarios, focused authorized edits/docs, actual red/green results and
unperformed checks. Given/When/Then vocabulary inside Iterate does not constitute
test-first fidelity. See the BDD cases in [examples](../resources/examples.md) and
source `bdd` in [provenance](../resources/provenance.json).

develop/references/prd.md.content:
# Implementation specification

Establish user outcome, current baseline, proposed increment and compatibility.
Put prerequisites and consequential blocking owner decisions first. Select one
preferred complete design using correctness, simplicity, maintainability, project
fit and likely usage; expose genuine business/access/domain unknowns rather than
leaving supported technical choices to the implementer.

Specify contracts, identities, time semantics, ambiguous/missing inputs, failure
behavior, exclusions, acceptance scenarios, docs and validation. Remove repetition,
placeholders and references to unavailable conversation context. Historical
cleanroom assumptions are not permission to remove current compatibility.

Return the concise developer handoff and bounded unknowns. Drafting does not
execute the specification, initialize a feature manifest, commit, or replace
Iterate's real-options architecture/user-approval checkpoint. See PRD examples
and source `code-review` in [provenance](../resources/provenance.json).

# Targeted prompt and contract editing

Identify the behavioral delta and actual upstream/downstream surfaces: generation
instructions, schemas/wire examples, validation, replay and versioning. Do not
invent missing extraction or evaluation layers.

Keep generation prompts focused on behavior, wire hints on exact shapes/examples,
and replay summaries on compact validated results. Edit only the affected surfaces
and synchronize their consumers. Preserve authority, uncertainty, redaction,
application-owned fields and accepted-output-only replay where applicable.

Add deterministic contract/example regression coverage where supported, respecting
the selected lifecycle's testing stage. Structural validity and generation quality
are different claims; model-backed checks require approved tooling/data/protocol.

Return coordinated authorized edits, rationale, actual regression evidence and
remaining generation uncertainty. In review-only requests make no edits. Source
`prompt` and worked cases are in the bundled provenance/examples resources.

Establish authoritative requirements/use cases, decision dates, superseded/conflicting
decisions, declared scope and current work-item metadata. Exhaust relevant pagination
or label incomplete coverage. Absence from one repository is not absence elsewhere.

Map primary delivery, supporting/enabling work and validation separately. Distinguish
implemented baseline, requested increment, partial coverage, ownership gap and
unknown state. A broad use-case reference or related code is not completion.
Refine an appropriate existing owner before proposing duplicate work. Preserve

separate from Iterate's CLI-owned feature backlog; no automatic state synchronization.

or construct research cohorts as a side effect. See source `backlog` and examples.

review/references/code.md.content:
# Code review

Review whether the declared change or current implementation is desirable,
well-placed, correct and maintainable. This is a source-grounded review, not an
automatic repository-wide audit or permission to apply the recommendations.

Use this mode to decide whether the declared implementation/change is acceptable.
When the requested outcome is instead a structural inventory and remediation
plan for a subsystem, select `smells`; a source sample does not establish a whole
repository review. General code explanations need neither assessment mode.

## Establish the review contract

- Identify the target and actual snapshot: supplied diff/PR and established base,
  or explicitly selected current-source scope. Account for workspace edits when
  those are the target. Without a base, do not claim a defect was introduced by
  an unknown change.
- Read current project instructions, the PRD or other requirements, relevant
  architectural direction and protected contracts. Trace changed code through its
  callers, tests, documentation and configuration as needed to assess consequences;
  distinguish supporting inspection from expanding the finding scope.
- Load available prior findings when re-reviewing. Establish which earlier scope
  and snapshot they described; do not invent a previous review when none is supplied.
- Establish existing users, public consumers and compatibility requirements.
  A historical prompt's pre-user assumption is not evidence about this project.
  If cleanroom/pre-user status is established, apply the cleanup policy below;
  otherwise preserve known contracts and label consequential unknowns.
- Separate failures caused only by the review environment from code defects.
  Missing `pyarrow` or another hard dependency in an atypical environment is not
  itself a finding. An undeclared required production dependency can be a finding
  when supported by packaging and runtime evidence. Disclose checks that could
  not run; continue independent source inspection without pretending they passed.

## Review in this order

1. **Intent:** Does the change solve the right problem? Is the feature, behavior
   or cleanup desirable under the requirements and likely use cases? Identify
   unnecessary or misdirected work before polishing its implementation.
2. **Architecture:** Is responsibility in the right place? Does the design fit the
   current project structure and intended direction, with sensible dependencies,
   APIs and module boundaries?
3. **Implementation:** Is behavior correct, maintainable and reasonably simple?
   Are tests proportionate and meaningful, documentation accurate, and the PRD,
   implementation, tests and docs consistent with one another?
4. **Polish:** Inspect naming, wording, consistency and important nits that improve
   clarity, maintainability or contributor onboarding. Do not let nits displace a
   more consequential intent or design issue.

## Coverage checklist

Use these as inspection lenses, not a finding quota. Substantiate claims with
actual use and a concrete consequence.

| Lens | What to establish |
|---|---|
| Dead, unused or underused code | Callers, registration, supported extension points and whether the remaining benefit justifies the surface. Low usage alone is not proof of dead code. |
| Generalization, specialization and overengineering | Whether abstractions, layers, options or one-off special cases serve real requirements rather than hypothetical users or obsolete designs. |
| Leaky abstractions | Whether callers must know implementation details or repair a boundary's incomplete contract. |
| Risky duplication | Repeated algorithms, schema knowledge, configuration or policies that can diverge; distinguish matching behavior from merely similar syntax. |
| Unnecessary complexity | Branching, modes, mutable state and indirection that make behavior or changes harder to reason about. |
| Documentation complexity | Overly verbose, duplicated or complicated docs that obscure the usable contract or increase synchronization work; retain necessary explanations. |
| Test design | Fragile, inconsistent or overengineered tests, implementation coupling, redundant setup and missing behavioral coverage. |
| Cross-file consistency | Conflicting coding standards or architectural approaches; assess the project's actual conventions rather than personal taste. |
| Layout and ownership | Whether directories, modules and responsibility boundaries are logical, discoverable and easy to follow. |
| Historical names and surfaces | Names, APIs, module boundaries and file organization reflecting former designs instead of today's intended design. |
| Contract alignment | Inconsistencies among the PRD, implementation, tests, docs and configuration, including missing or contradictory acceptance behavior. |
| Removal opportunities | Unnecessary code, tests, docs, configuration, compatibility branches, old references or dead paths; use the established compatibility policy. |
| Reviewability | Changes too large, broad or mixed-purpose to assess effectively. Name the separable concerns and recommend a coherent split; disclose what remains unreviewed. |

Do not spend findings on formatting, routine lint or other issues correctly handled
by automation. Inspect the automation when the diff shows it is missing,
misconfigured or inconsistently applied; report that underlying gap instead of
enumerating every mechanically detectable symptom.

## Choose a decisive, complete remedy

Consider the reasonable solution space, then recommend **one preferred solution**
for each important issue. Balance correctness, simplicity, maintainability,
project consistency and likely users/use cases. The smallest textual patch is
not the objective: prefer the cleanest, clearest, lowest-complexity design that
fully addresses the cause, including relevant tests/docs/configuration.

Make the handoff sufficiently prescriptive for a junior developer: identify what
to remove or move, which boundary should own behavior, what contracts remain,
and how to verify the outcome. Avoid "consider refactoring" without a concrete
direction. Offer alternatives only for a real unresolved tradeoff the available
context cannot settle; explain the decision-changing evidence rather than
leaving an open-ended menu.

When cleanroom/pre-user status and no compatibility obligations are established:

- Do not preserve legacy behavior, old references, dead paths, defensive
  compatibility layers, deprecated APIs or migration mechanisms solely for
  hypothetical existing users. Recommend removing obsolete surfaces rather than
  adding another compatibility wrapper.
- Prefer fixing worthwhile nits and optional cleanup now, especially clarity,
  consistency, maintainability and onboarding improvements. Deferral needs a
  concrete reason such as disproportionate effort or a genuinely separate concern.
- State whether this assumption changes each recommendation. No existing users
  does not erase current behavioral, security, data or architectural requirements.

Outside cleanroom, honor actual consumers and migration obligations. Unknown
compatibility is not removal permission. "Fix now" describes the recommendation,
not authorization for the reviewer to edit code or widen the task.

## Finding contract

Each actionable finding includes:

1. A stable ID, short title, verified file/line location and the actual evidence.
2. **Urgency** and **feedback type**, using the separate scales below.
3. The issue and why it matters: concrete behavioral, maintenance or contributor
   consequence, not a broad stylistic assertion.
4. One preferred complete fix and why it balances simplicity and completeness;
   identify relevant contracts and behavioral validation.
5. Whether it is worth fixing now, with the reason for any deferral.
6. Compatibility assumptions and whether established no-users/no-compatibility
   status changes the fix or its timing.
7. Introduced, worsened or relevant pre-existing status when a real comparison
   supports it; otherwise say introduction is unknown.

| Urgency | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Must fix before merging | A merge blocker supported by the requirements or consequences. |
| Should fix now | Important correction or cleanup that should accompany the change. |
| Optional, but recommended now | Non-blocking improvement worth doing in this revision; default for worthwhile cleanroom nits. |
| Optional, can defer | A justified separate or lower-value improvement; give the reason. |

| Feedback type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| TODO | Must be addressed before merge. |
| Question | Needs an answer, but may not require code changes. |
| Follow-up | Worth considering separately; explain why separation is appropriate. |
| Nit | Small improvement with a clarity, consistency or maintainability benefit. |

Keep urgency separate from impact severity and the structural audit's S0–S3 scale.
Use compatible labels: do not call a deferrable item a mandatory TODO. A question
is for a consequential unknown, not a substitute for making a supported decision.

## Re-review and delivery

Return a consolidated review, not just an appended list of new findings. Recheck
prior claims against current raw evidence: update still-open items, resolve
verified fixes, withdraw stale/unsupported claims with reasons, and merge duplicates
while retaining their IDs as aliases. Add new findings without losing earlier
in-scope concerns. Mark prior items outside the revised scope as not reassessed;
do not silently drop them or call them fixed.

Use the requested output format, including valid JSON when requested, and rank
actionable findings by consequence and urgency. Include scope/snapshot, comparison
limits, reviewed and unreviewed areas, and actual checks with passed/failed/not-run
or blocked status. Do not claim full coverage from a sample. No actionable findings
is a valid result. Do not edit files or post the review without separate authority.

review/references/smells.md.content:
# Consequence-grounded structural audit

Audit the declared source for structures that make change, testing, security or
operations materially harder. The supplied Python source is a completed review
report, not the separately referenced *Code Review Guide to Code Smells in Python*.
Its findings illustrate reasoning and remedies; they are not current defects,
universal size thresholds or instructions to refactor those historical files.
The separate guide remains unavailable; do not claim to have applied its full
catalog. See the [source coverage map](source-coverage.md) for that boundary.

Use this mode when the requested outcome is structural diagnosis and a maintenance
plan for a declared scope. Assessing whether a particular implementation/change
is acceptable belongs to `code`. A generic question about smells is an explanation,
not authorization to inspect a repository or refactor its code.

## Scope and inventory

- Declare subsystem/repository boundaries, current workspace or commit snapshot,
  language, architecture, public invariants and compatibility requirements.
  Inspect relevant callers, tests and configuration to understand the target.
- For the report-equivalent Python scope, inventory **all production and
  repository-support Python files**, including relevant hidden support directories
  such as CI scripts. Exclude tests, virtual/generated environments and
  non-production experiments from the finding scope unless the user requests them.
  They may still provide supporting evidence; label that distinction. Honor an
  explicitly different scope or language rather than forcing Python defaults.
- Track every eligible file as reviewed, partially reviewed or unreviewed. Calculate
  file/line counts from the actual snapshot if reporting them, explain the counting
  basis, and separate inventory totals from inspected totals. Never reuse the
  historical report's 56 files, 10,012 lines or July 22, 2026 line references.
- Inventory responsibility and mutable-state clusters, collaborators, repeated
  algorithms and schema knowledge, and changes requiring coordinated edits. Trace
  actual uses before judging the design; a missing source limits the claim.

## Evidence threshold and counterexamples

A finding needs an identifiable maintenance, change-locality, testability,
security or operational consequence. Explain which change becomes scattered,
which state or policy can diverge, which boundary leaks, or which invariant is at
risk. Size and branch counts can support the explanation but do not prove it.

Do not label DTOs, protocols, package markers, boundary adapters or cohesive long
routines solely because of their size or shape. Check whether a data object names
a real contract, a protocol has useful consumers, a facade preserves a purposeful
public boundary, or a wrapper adds validation/normalization rather than mere
forwarding. Declarative constants and table-driven step definitions can centralize
variation rather than create a smell. Broad catches at CLI/command/logging
boundaries can be proportionate exception translation; inspect their effect, not
just their syntax. Likewise, a lengthy lookup or budget algorithm may be cohesive.

Separate a supported design consequence from a preference and from a direct
correctness defect. State counterevidence and uncertain runtime consequences;
do not elevate "could diverge" to a demonstrated failure without evidence.

## Diagnostic families and concrete probes

These probes retain the pressure points illustrated by F01–F10 in the supplied
report. Apply those relevant to the current scope, not a requirement to find all
ten or to introduce the named design patterns everywhere.

| Family / source pattern | Inspect and substantiate | Preferred direction when supported |
|---|---|---|
| Bloaters / Large Class; Divergent Change; Couplers / Solution Sprawl (F01) | Unrelated responsibility clusters such as orchestration, retry, tool execution, persistence, failure translation and result construction sharing broad mutable state or collaborators. Show independent reasons to change and focused-test costs. | Keep a purposeful public facade, extracting cohesive collaborators at actual ownership seams rather than splitting by line count. |
| Dispensables / Duplicated Code; Object-Orientation Abusers / Combinatorial Explosion (F02) | Repeated state machines with differing counters, terminal behavior, repairs or validation. Compare transitions and genuinely different completion policies, not just similar loops. | Extract one shared transition loop with a narrow policy/callback and small distinct completion handlers; avoid multiplying boolean modes. |
| Bloaters / Long Parameter List and Data Clumps; Duplicated Code (F03) | Primitive run/step/error/event fields repeatedly forwarded through helpers and serializers, especially a failure path that bypasses the normal recorder. Trace defaults, redaction, indexing and persistence ownership. | Introduce a cohesive event draft/context value and one recorder for index assignment, serialization and persistence; retain the required storage schema at the boundary. |
| Change Preventers / Shotgun Surgery; Long Method (F04) | One setting duplicated across allowed keys, typed settings, precedence, coercion, validation, deployment env names, render arguments and templates. Enumerate the coordinated-edit sites. | Own field/default/env/coercion metadata once and consume it in runtime/deployment paths; separate scalar parsing from cross-field invariants. |
| Bloaters / Long Method, Long Parameter List and Data Clumps (F05) | A packaging routine mixing acquisition, normalization, token estimates, repeated whole-context reconstruction, truncation search, parallel mutable accumulators, metrics and payload presentation. Identify the coupled stages and identity/budget fields. | Use a cohesive request/context value, a budget allocator returning blocks/outcomes, and a separate public payload presenter. Do not fragment a cohesive budget algorithm solely because it is long. |
| Long Method; Object-Orientation Abusers / Conditional Complexity (F06) | A reconciliation pipeline mixing dynamic-shape parsing, source lookup, fuzzy correction, mutation, final-attempt policy, status counters and diagnostics. Trace branches updating the same accumulators. | Parse typed candidates, reconcile each to a result, then reduce results into payload/metadata; make differing mismatch policy explicit rather than a threaded boolean. |
| Divergent Change; Long Method (F07) | Graph construction, nested closures, parse-state history, validation, repair prompts, evidence reconciliation and safe/final result projection sharing a module. Check whether temporary state is per-run or closure-held. | Retain the registry-facing factory where it is a contract; separate validation/reconciliation and projection, with explicit per-run validation context. |
| Conditional Complexity; Couplers / Inappropriate Intimacy (F08) | Orchestration branching on internal tool dictionaries while also owning transitions, retry guidance, templates, events and evidence-source presentation. Look for guards reconstructing argument shapes independently. | Adapt raw tool content once into stable outcome values, isolate the acquisition transition policy, and keep presentation outside it. |
| Dispensables / Oddball Solution and Duplicated Code (F09) | Multiple row adapters using mappings, indexing or `asDict()` with inconsistent copying, required fields and exception contracts. Verify that their domain requirements actually match. | Own one validated row adaptation contract at the storage/provider boundary; let domain mappers consume it without leaking provider-specific shape knowledge. |
| Object-Orientation Abusers / Conditional Complexity (F10) | An expanding assertion catalog requiring fields, validation, branching, result changes and CLI rendering, particularly domain rules mixed with generic checks. | Use typed assertion specifications and a small evaluator registry only when it consolidates real variation; keep domain-specific assertions separate from generic path/equality/list checks. |

One finding may span several families. Name the actual smell and consequence,
not every possible catalog label. These source patterns are not a complete Python
smell guide or exclusive list of problems the current source may exhibit.

## Remedy design and preserved behavior

Recommend one preferred remedy that lowers total complexity and change risk,
not merely the smallest patch or the greatest number of extractions. Typed
values, registries, adapters and state machines must centralize ownership or make
a contract clearer, rather than relocate the same branches behind indirection.
Avoid hypothetical extension mechanisms and additional boolean mode combinations.

Identify the behavior the remedy must preserve: transition and event ordering,
retry/terminal rules, errors and diagnostics, redaction, serialization defaults,
indexes, append-only schemas, configuration precedence/coercion, budget outcomes,
safe outputs, public APIs and security boundaries, as relevant. Preserve known
consumers and compatibility; do not infer cleanroom from the source report. If
the current task establishes cleanroom, obsolete compatibility surfaces can be
removed, but present behavioral/data/security requirements still apply.

State the behavioral validation needed for those invariants and whether it already
exists, was run or remains proposed. Pure structural changes can use existing
characterization tests; do not manufacture a failing test to justify a refactor.
The audit does not itself authorize tests with external effects or implementation.

## Findings and severity

Each finding includes a stable ID and title, S-level, family/specific smell,
verified current file/line locations, structural evidence, concrete consequence,
one preferred remedy with rationale, protected invariants and needed validation.
When using metrics, derive them from the inspected source. Do not copy historical
IDs, metrics, locations or severity judgments as newly verified findings.

| Structural severity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| S3 | Correctness or operational risk. |
| S2 | Significant design risk. |
| S1 | Maintainability concern. |
| S0 | Observation; distinguish it from actionable defects. |

Keep S0–S3 separate from merge urgency, feedback type and Debate impact labels.
Do not infer one scale from another. Rank findings by supported consequence;
no minimum count or severity distribution is required.

## Report and remediation order

Deliver the requested format; the report-equivalent default includes:

1. **Scope and method:** snapshot, inclusions/exclusions, actual inventory/inspection
   counts when available, evidence sources and missing guide or source limitations.
2. **Executive summary:** useful existing boundaries and the principal structural
   pressure points, not a generic verdict or a claim that everything needs rewriting.
3. **Ranked findings:** the evidence/remedy contract above, with multiple verified
   locations when the consequence crosses files.
4. **File-by-file coverage ledger:** every in-scope file maps to finding IDs,
   "No material finding", partial review or unreviewed with a reason. "No material
   finding" means inspected structure is proportionate to its role, not perfection;
   it cannot describe an unread file. Note useful counterexamples where relevant.
5. **Dependency-aware remediation:** explain which seam reduces risk for later
   changes, then order independent and smaller work. For example, one event
   draft/recorder can precede runner-loop extraction; configuration centralization
   can proceed independently; typed item/acquisition pipelines and smaller row/
   assertion consolidation follow where their dependencies justify it. This is
   a planning example, not a prescribed sequence for every project.
6. **Checks and limits:** actual versus proposed/unperformed validation and
   incomplete inspections. No findings is a valid bounded result.

For a revised audit, reassess prior findings against the new snapshot and retain
their dispositions/IDs without duplicating or silently dropping concerns. Keep
the audit read-only; proposed remediation does not authorize a refactor or posting.

# Review source coverage

Maintenance reference for the two supplied review materials, inspected in full
on November 4, 2026. Routine review loads only its selected method, not this map.
This is an instruction-coverage assessment, not evidence of model performance.

## Source identity and interpretation

| Supplied file | SHA-256 | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| `code_review.md` | `246c283cd34709915fc74fbe0c8911400b8e36badf1cc65f727f78d30ac979b7` | 66-line review instruction set. Its cleanroom premise applies only when established for the actual target. |
| `code_smell.md` | `1ef0fe6c8593252461516c02ed53401b370719cc4dc0dc4d6bc945899dc7c5a7` | 270-line completed Python review report. Its methodology, reasoning patterns and output structure transfer; its target-specific findings do not. |

excerpt-only checks to the full supplied files. External prompt-library paths
are not runtime dependencies and the source files themselves are not bundled.

The initial 28-line method references retained the headline boundaries, scales
and concise finding contracts, but compressed away explicit inspection lenses,
remedy decisions, counterexamples and reporting detail. The expanded references
restore those behaviors without making `SKILL.md` a copy of both source files.

## Code-review requirements

Locations refer to the source instruction's lines, not a current code target.
Every row maps to an explicit section of [code review](code.md).

| Ignore environment-only missing hard dependencies | 3 | Establish the review contract; distinguish reviewer setup from a supported production packaging defect. |

| Balance correctness, simplicity, maintainability, project consistency and users/use cases; not the smallest patch | 9 | Choose a decisive, complete remedy; optimize the complete design rather than textual change size. |

| Intent → architecture → implementation → polish | 13–18 | Review in this order; desirable change before placement, correctness and important nits. |
| Dead, unused or underused code | 22 | Coverage checklist; verify real use, registration and benefit rather than infer deadness from frequency. |
| Unnecessary generalization/specialization and obvious overengineering | 23–24 | Coverage checklist; actual requirements versus speculative or obsolete surfaces. |
